title: Apple working on Beats-branded game controllers, report confirms
content:
Macworld





A few weeks ago, code references in the first macOS 26.7 release candidate pointed to the imminent launch of two game controller devices. (There were also clues in there to a set of camera-equipped AirPods, but that’s another story.) And a new report has now added further detail about the launch plans for these products.
In the latest edition of his Power On newsletter, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman confirms that Apple has indeed been working on these iPhone gaming accessories “for a bit over a year” and is keen to join what the company views as a lucrative market. He doesn’t name any sources for this, simply saying, “Here’s what I know.” But Gurman’s sources tend to be solid, as you can see with the accuracy of his last-minute iPhone Duo leak just before the launch event last week.
The “interesting part” of Gurman’s new report (his words, not mine) is that the game controllers are being developed and, if released, will likely launch under the Beats brand rather than Apple’s.
“The company has increasingly been using Beats as a way to experiment with new product categories and capitalize on the third-party accessories market without putting certain types of products under the more premium Apple brand,” he explains.
This, he argues, is a wise move when developing gaming products. A game controller for the iPhone would need to be relatively affordable in order to reach a wide audience, but as we saw at last week’s Surprise and Shine event, Apple prefers devices that are rather more premium when launching under its own brand.
A glance at the Beats section of Apple’s website illustrates this approach. The cheapest Apple-branded wireless earbuds you can buy are the AirPods 5, at $129, while the cheapest Beats equivalents are the Beats Flex, at $70. Similarly, the AirPods Max 2 are $549, whereas the similarly featured Beats Studio Pro are $350.
Going with the Beats branding also makes sense from a cultural/lifestyle point of view, Gurman claims. Beats is a younger and altogether hipper brand. Apple, by contrast, doesn’t appear to “get” gaming.
We should emphasise that Gurman is merely claiming that Apple is and has been working on game controller accessories for the iPhone,a nd there’s no guarantee that they’ll ever launch. But if they do, he’s confident that they’ll have a “b” on them rather than an Apple logo.

title: Apple Releases watchOS 27 With Siri AI, New Watch Face, Smart Stack Improvements and More
content:
Apple today released watchOS 27, the newest version of the operating system that runs on the Apple Watch. ‌watchOS 27‌ is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later, the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later, and the Apple Watch SE 3.


‌watchOS 27‌ can be downloaded for free on a compatible device through the Settings app on the watch.

Siri AI, a more capable version of ‌Siri‌ that uses personal context and onscreen awareness to help you get things done. There's a new ‌Siri‌ Modular watch face, updates to Smart Stack, improvements to Liquid Glass, and a consolidated Find My app. Apple's release notes for the update are below.
Siri AI
- A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge
- New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on paired iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later
- Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud

Apple Intelligence across apps
- Workout Buddy delivers motivation with new insights and is now available without your iPhone nearby when you have a Wi-Fi or cellular connection
- Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number

Cycle Tracking
- Cycle deviation notifications that are suggestive of perimenopause can be received by those age 40 and over

Watch Faces
- Siri Modular face features a rectangular complication that mirrors the top widget of the Smart Stack, which dynamically updates to show the most relevant widget, as well as a Siri complication to quickly invoke Siri

Smart Stack
- Single-handed tap gesture enables you to tap your index finger and thumb together once to select a widget in the Smart Stack, even if your other hand is occupied
- New suggestion widgets will be surfaced when most relevant to you, including a Parked Car location, birthday reminders for a close contact, balance changes on a transit card, Noise app after a loud noise notification, and more

System Improvements
- Dynamic app grid highlights your most popular and recently used apps
- Find My app is now consolidated into one app to show People, Devices, and Items with a map-centric interface
- Media playback now starts faster
- Workout app makes distance calculations during treadmill workouts even more accurate from the first step of every walk or run
- Fitness app features more accurate route maps after workouts
- Battery extension notifications may be proactively offered to disable certain features to increase battery life, including gestures, Start Workout reminders, and Raise to Speak method of invoking Siri
- Shazam in the Smart Stack and Music Recognition app identifies songs offline without an internet connection and delivers results automatically when you're back online
Siri AI in ‌watchOS 27‌ requires an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, which includes the iPhone 15 Pro models, the iPhone Air, and all iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone 18 models.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate vs Tahoe: What’s new and should you upgrade?
content:
Macworld






Should you upgrade to macOS Golden Gate?
Upgrade to macOS Golden Gate if you have an Apple Silicon Mac and want the latest Apple Intelligence features. Golden Gate is especially appealing for heavy Spotlight users, Safari users, Shortcuts fans, and families who use parental controls.
Note that some features need newer hardware. All Macs with Apple Silicon can run macOS 27, but certain advanced AI features require newer chips and more memory. 
macOS 27 Golden Gate arrived on September 14, bringing a much smarter Siri, refinements to the Liquid Glass interface, faster performance, improved search and a range of new Apple Intelligence features to the Mac.
Golden Gate builds on macOS 26 Tahoe rather than reinventing macOS all over again. The biggest changes come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, alongside improvements to Safari, Spotlight, Photos, parental controls and everyday system performance.
But how much has actually changed since macOS 26 Tahoe, and is macOS 27 worth installing? Here’s how Golden Gate compares with macOS Tahoe and which Macs will benefit most from upgrading.


What are the biggest new features in macOS 27 Golden Gate?

				
					

				
			
An overview of the features coming in macOS 27
.
Foundry




Here is our pick of the macOS Golden Gate features that we think will make the biggest difference.
Siri AI could finally become genuinely useful
Golden Gate’s biggest upgrade is the complete overhaul of Siri. Instead of relying mainly on simple commands, Siri can understand personal context, search across files and photos using natural language, compare information, answer questions about what’s on screen and perform more complex actions across apps. This could be the most significant Siri upgrade since the assistant first launched.
Smarter Search and Spotlight
Apple has rebuilt the indexing system that powers Spotlight, Mail and Photos. The result should be faster searches, more relevant results and a better understanding of what users are actually looking for. Since search is something most Mac users rely on throughout the day, this under-the-hood improvement could prove to be one of Golden Gate’s most useful changes.
Safari gets useful automation features
Safari gains several AI-powered and automation features designed to reduce everyday friction. Tabs can be organized into related groups, Notify Me can monitor webpages and alert you when content changes, and Safari can automatically update compromised passwords on supported websites.
More powerful AI photo editing
Golden Gate also brings more advanced editing tools to Photos. Users can extend images beyond their original boundaries, adjust perspective and composition, remove unwanted objects more effectively and create new imagery with Image Playground. Some of these features will arrive in later macOS 27 updates rather than being available at launch.
Much stronger parental controls
Family features receive a substantial upgrade too. Parents can approve websites through Ask to Browse, approve new contacts, monitor a wider range of potentially harmful content and use updated Screen Time recommendations. For families with children using Apple devices, these are among the most practical improvements in macOS 27.


						

							


What are the key differences between Golden Gate vs Tahoe?
Siri is dramatically more capable, adding personal context, Visual Intelligence, document comparison, and natural-language automation.
Liquid Glass has been refined, with better readability, transparency controls, coloured sidebar icons, and improved visual consistency.
Parental controls have been expanded significantly, including website approvals, contact approvals, and enhanced Communication Safety.
Safari is proactive, adding page monitoring, AI tab management, and automatic password replacement.
Search has major backend improvements, enabling it to deliver faster and more accurate results across Spotlight, Mail, and Photos.


						

							






FeaturemacOS TahoemacOS Golden Gate

Refined Liquid Glass interfaceIntroduced Liquid Glass design languageBetter readability, transparency controls, coloured sidebar icons, improved window consistency
Expanded Siri AI capabilitiesBasic Apple Intelligence integrationPersonal context awareness, Visual Intelligence, file discovery, document comparison, Shortcut creation
Stronger parental controlsScreen Time and child safety tools became easier to set up Ask to Browse, contact approvals, expanded content monitoring, improved recommendations
Smarter Safari automationImproved web app supportAI tab grouping by topic, Notify Me monitoring, automatic password replacement
New AI photo editing toolsPhotos app gained Clean Up feature, AI-powered photo search, Image Playground integrated with ChatGPTGenerative image expansion, perspective changes, smarter object removal, enhanced Image Playground
Performance and search improvementsExisting Spotlight improvementsRebuilt indexing engine, faster search, improved Mail and Photos relevance

 macOS 27 compared to macOS 26






What’s new in macOS Golden Gate?
macOS 27 Golden Gate represents a significant step forward for the Mac, with a strong focus on Apple Intelligence, refinements to the Liquid Glass interface introduced in macOS 26 Tahoe, and major improvements to search, Safari, Photos and parental controls. It also marks the end of Intel Mac support, with Golden Gate available only for Macs with Apple silicon.
The main changes include:
Enhanced parental controls: Stronger family-safety tools, including improved website, contact and Screen Time controls. For families with children using Apple devices, these are among the most practical improvements in macOS 27.
Siri AI: A much more capable Siri with better conversational understanding, personal context and onscreen awareness.
Improved Apple Intelligence: New AI features that can work across apps and surface relevant information.
Faster performance: Quicker app launches, searches, AirDrop transfers and networking, alongside better overall responsiveness.
Smarter Spotlight: Faster, more relevant search results across Spotlight, Mail and Photos.
AI photo editing: More powerful editing tools in Photos, including image expansion, improved object removal and generative features.
Liquid Glass refinements: Improvements to the interface introduced with macOS Tahoe, with better readability and consistency.
Safari upgrades: New automation features, smarter tab organization and improved password management.


						

							


Is the Liquid Glass design any better?

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS Tahoe arrived in 2025 with the new Liquid Glass graphical sheen on the interface. This was rolled out across all Apple products, but it’s fair to say that it wasn’t entirely loved by everyone. The refracted light effect could be quite smart looking, but some complained it was harder to see things clearly.
Apple seems to have paid attention, as macOS Golden Gate has been refined to deal with these concerns. It’s using a new process, and Apple announced that “to ensure exceptional readability, we tuned Liquid Glass so it diffuses complex content behind it much more effectively, while also creating more depth and separation.”
There’s now the addition of a slider in Settings that allows users to decide on the level of clarity or tint of Liquid Glass, so you can tailor it to your own preferences. 
Apple has also tweaked the interface in macOS Golden Gate with the addition of toolbars across the tops of apps where there are a number of control options. This adds a bit of needed structure and should keep things legible on the page. Sidebar icons have also been given back their color, so it’s more instantly distinguishable which option is selected. All app windows will now feature the same rounded corners, to give a more consistent look, and icons have also been given a spruce-up to make them appear fresh. 


						

							


Will Golden Gate make my Mac faster?
One of the main focuses of macOS Golden Gate is system performance, with Apple reworking a number of the underlying processes that power the operating system. Early reports from beta testers suggest that the update makes Macs feel noticeably faster and more responsive, with quicker app launches, snappier Spotlight searches, faster AirDrop transfers and improved networking. Some testers have even reported noticeable speed improvements on older supported Macs.
Apple has also improved support for external displays, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth, while refinements to the Liquid Glass interface should make macOS feel smoother and more consistent in everyday use. In our own testing of the Golden Gate beta on a MacBook Neo with an A18 Pro chip and 8GB of RAM, Siri performance was perfectly acceptable. There was some processing time when handling requests, but no obvious lag attributable to the chip or limited memory.
Search is another area where Apple has made significant changes. A revamped indexing process should provide more accurate Spotlight results, as well as improve the relevance of searches in Mail and Photos. That is particularly welcome after some macOS Tahoe users experienced Spotlight-related freezes, including Macworld staff. As we detailed in System freezes plagued my Mac for months. A simple fix finally solved it, one Mac was found to have nearly 10,000 corrupted files in its Spotlight metadata folder, causing repeated system stalls. Golden Gate’s reworked indexing system is intended to make search faster and more reliable from the outset.
If you’re running an Apple silicon Mac, Golden Gate should therefore offer a tangible performance improvement, particularly when launching apps, searching, transferring files and working across the system. There is one important limitation, though: macOS Golden Gate drops support for Intel-based Macs altogether, so Intel Mac owners won’t be able to install the update.


						

							


Parents get more control over child accounts

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple has always been a company that takes security and privacy seriously, and that looks to be enhanced with the additional child-safety features in macOS Golden Gate. Working with the American Academy of Pediatrics, Apple has created a child safety set of tools that starts with a setup guide that allows them to decide on the apps their progeny can use on their device. 
Of course, this capability was already in place in macOS Tahoe, but now Golden Gate adds an important improvement with Ask to Browse, whereby any new website a child wants to access in Safari has to be approved by the parents (usually via Messages). There’s also an approval restriction for any new contacts a child wants to connect with. Communication Safety now acts not only as a constant monitor for any sexual images or videos that the child is being sent or wants to send, but also for gory or violent content. The idea is to give parents more tools to protect their kids from the darker and more unsavoury elements of digital life. Yes, the settings will mainly apply to iPads and iPhones, but they can be controlled and monitored from your Mac.
Time Allowances provide parents with the ability to set daily limits on three categories of content – Entertainment, Social Media, and Gaming – but it can confusing to know what these should be. Apple now includes recommended amounts for each, as researched by the American Academy of Pediatrics, so they have a good idea of what’s healthy. These are determined by age and can be manually adjusted by the parent at any time, as well as the option to set up schedules that vary depending on the day. 


						

							


How much smarter is Siri in Golden Gate?
Siri in macOS Golden Gate is significantly more capable thanks to new Apple Intelligence models. You can ask Siri to find files, photos or other information simply by describing what you’re looking for. 
Apple says that the new models work with the principles of Personal Context understanding (all the things relative to you) and Broad world knowledge (all information on the web) to give you the answers you want to questions, be they which shed to buy or where to find those photos of that trip to Paris. 
Visual Intelligence allows you to highlight something on your screen and ask Siri AI for information about it, and there’s the dedicated Siri app that allows you to keep all of your conversations in one place, no matter if they were on your iPhone, iPad or Mac. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




There’s plenty of scope for Siri AI, with the WWDC demonstration showing the ability to highlight files then ask it to compare them and show you the results, you can also open a context menu and use the Ask Siri option to find out more information about something. Having trouble creating Shortcuts? In macOS Golden Gate you can describe what you want and Siri AI will build it for you.  
As with any AI software, we’ll need more time with the final release to judge how reliably these features work in everyday use, but they represent a major step forward from macOS Tahoe. 


						

							


Better Writing Tools in Mail and Messages
Apple Intelligence first appeared in macOS Sequoia, but there were delays in features being rolled out, so it felt more like the AI era arrived with macOS Tahoe. Writing Tools is probably one of the most used of the AI upgrades, and with macOS Golden Gate these get another level of capabilities thanks to the new AI models. 
In Mail and Messages you can now not only generate content from a prompt, but Siri AI will tailor it to match the language and styling you’d normally use with that particular person. Say, for example, you want to send your client a proposal, then Siri AI will look at previous interactions between you and them and match the style – presumably a formal one. While, if you want to let a friend know that you’re having a BBQ and want them to come along, Siri AI will produce a suitably amiable and informal draft. 
It can also analyse any writing you’ve done and give tips on how it could be improved or made to better suit the situation in which it will be used. 


						

							


What’s new in Safari?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple’s browser gets the AI treatment in macOS Golden Gate, with some nice touches that can smooth out life online. The app can automatically group tabs into related topics, which can make researching things a bit more organised.
If you’re waiting for a news story or box office to open, then the new Notify Me feature will be a godsend. Simply tell Safari to watch the page, then you can carry on with other things while it constantly checks and then notifies you when the change occurs.


						

							


Change your passwords with Siri AI
If you’re tired of constantly being bombarded by notifications that several of your passwords have been compromised in some security breach, but don’t have the time to sort it out – help is at hand. Apple states that you can instruct Safari to automatically go to all those affected sites, log in to your accounts, then create new safe passwords which it stores in the Passwords app. 


						

							


What new AI photo tools are included?

				
					

				
			
Apple




You can’t have an AI updated without it somehow being related to photo editing, and that’s the case with macOS Golden Gate. The new Apple Intelligence models allow for some impressive editing and image creation. You can expand existing images, with the AI generating the extra data to make it look like it was always there. 
There’s also the ability to change the angle and perspective of an image, essentially meaning you can recompose the shot after the fact. As you’d expect, there’s also improved ways to remove items from the shots too, creating the perfect moment that never really happened. 
Image playground also gets beefed up in macOS Golden Gate, with even more ways to auto-generate images from simple prompts, then iteratively alter them by conversing with the AI. Apple did state that this would have daily limits though, with higher allowances linked to your iCloud+ subscription. 


						

							


Which Macs will run macOS 27 Golden Gate
You’ll be able to upgrade to macOS Golden Gate if you have any of the following hardware:
MacBook Neo (2026)
MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)
Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)
Apple does state that some of the high-end AI features will require more modern hardware – M3 and 12GB RAM or better – but this is limited to things like improved diction and the ability to create voices for Siri, which we’re thinking shouldn’t hamper too many people. 


						

							


When was macOS Golden Gate released?
Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on September 14, 2026, as a free software update for compatible Macs.
Siri AI is rolling out initially in English, while some other Apple Intelligence features are due to arrive in future macOS 27 updates. These include the new Spatial Reframing and Extend tools in Photos, as well as the enhanced Clean Up tool.


						

							


macOS Golden Gate vs Tahoe: Is it worth upgrading?
If your Mac supports macOS Golden Gate, there are plenty of reasons to upgrade. The biggest improvements come from Siri AI and Apple Intelligence, but faster performance, improved search, refinements to Liquid Glass and better parental controls should benefit users even if AI isn’t their main reason for updating.
Owners of Apple silicon Macs will get the most from Golden Gate, although some of its most advanced features won’t be available on every Mac and a handful of headline additions are arriving in later updates.
Read How to update macOS.

title: iOS 27.1: New Features to Expect and Release Date
content:
Apple's press release for the iPhone Duo last week said the device will ship with iOS 27.1, which essentially confirms the software update's release timing.


iPhone Duo launches on Friday, October 23, so we can expect iOS 27.1 to be released by that date at the latest — likely several days earlier.

iOS 27 will be released to the public today, and the first beta of iOS 27.1 will likely follow soon after.

New Features to Expect

During its iPhone event last week, Apple announced that Siri AI will be available in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish starting in October, and this expanded language support beyond English will likely arrive with iOS 27.1 based on that timeframe, as the software update itself will likely be released in October.


Apple recently said that two new features will not be available in the initial iOS 27 release, including suggestions like "Add to Reminders" and "Add to Notes" in the Messages app and the ability to automatically fix compromised passwords with a single tap in the Passwords app. Apple merely said these features will arrive in a "future software update," and iOS 27.1 will likely be the earliest opportunity for that to happen.

And of course, iOS 27.1 supports the iPhone Duo's unique foldable interface.

title: AirPods 4 vs. AirPods 5 Buyer's Guide
content:
Apple announced the AirPods 5 earlier this month, giving its entry-level earbuds Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) as standard for the first time. The AirPods 5 start at $129, a $149 model adds a Wireless Charging Case, and both versions arrive in stores on Friday, September 18.


The launch also resets the way Apple tiers its cheapest earbuds. With the AirPods 4, the $50 step up from $129 to $179 bought ANC along with a wireless charging case. With the ‌AirPods 5‌, noise cancellation comes at the entry price and now there is only a $20 step up to the next tier.

Here's everything that differs between the AirPods 4 and the ‌AirPods 5‌:

How Big Is the Upgrade?

The ‌AirPods 5‌ retain the H2 chip that debuted in the AirPods Pro 2 back in 2022, rather than the new headphone chip that had been rumored, and they retain Bluetooth 5.3, the same open-ear design, the same custom high-excursion driver and high dynamic range amplifier, and identical dimensions and weight down to the gram. Personalized Spatial Audio, Adaptive EQ, Voice Isolation, Personalized Volume, and Siri Interactions all came to the AirPods 4 two years ago.

Noise cancellation is the headline upgrade, and now included regardless of which 2026 model you choose. Apple says the ‌AirPods 5‌ remove up to 50% more external noise than the AirPods 4 with ANC, which it attributes to a redesigned acoustic architecture, and the same architecture underpins the claims of richer sound and a more natural Transparency mode. Durability improves from IP54 to IP57, so the earbuds and case are now rated for immersion rather than just splashes. Studio-quality audio recording is also new.

Should You Upgrade?

If you already own the AirPods 4 with ANC, there is not a strong case to upgrade. You already have Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode, Conversation Awareness, Live Translation, a wireless charging case with a ‌Find My‌ speaker, and the same H2 chip, so the $149 model would give you stronger noise cancellation, a higher IP rating, an extra hour of listening time, and swipe volume controls.

The case is stronger if you own the standard AirPods 4. Noise cancellation, Transparency mode, Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, and Live Translation are all missing from that model, and the ‌AirPods 5‌ add every one of them at the same $129 you paid two years ago. The same goes for anyone still using the AirPods 3 or AirPods 2, where the jump also brings the newer fit, the H2 chip, USB-C, and Personalized Spatial Audio.

For new buyers, the ‌AirPods 5‌ are the clear default choice. The AirPods 4 are the better value option only when heavily discounted.

AirPods Pro 3 are still the earbuds to buy. By contrast, if in-ear tips irritate you or you want to stay more aware of your environment, the ‌AirPods 5‌ now offer a far more capable version of the design you will prefer.

using our Deals roundup.

Which AirPods 5 Model to Buy?

The difference between the two ‌AirPods 5‌ models is significant despite the $20 gap. The Wireless Charging Case works with Qi chargers and the Apple Watch charger, contains a speaker that makes it much easier to find in the ‌Find My‌ app, and comes with an extra hour of listening time on a charge and two extra hours across the case.

title: iOS 27 vs iOS 26: These are the biggest reasons to upgrade
content:
Macworld






Should you update to iOS 27?
iOS 27 is worth upgrading for users who want a smarter Siri, new AI-powered photo tools, stronger security and faster everyday performance. Owners of the iPhone 15 Pro and newer models will benefit most from Apple Intelligence, while older supported iPhones miss out on some of the more advanced AI features.
iOS 27 arrived on September 14, 2026, bringing one of the biggest upgrades to Siri yet, along with faster performance, new AI-powered photo editing tools, stronger security and a long list of improvements across Apple’s apps.
While iOS 26 introduced headline changes including the Liquid Glass redesign, Call Screening and the first wave of Apple Intelligence features, iOS 27 is more about making the iPhone smarter, faster and more useful. Siri AI is the star of the update, but there are also significant improvements to Photos, Safari, Passwords, parental controls and more.
So, how does iOS 27 compare with iOS 26, what do you actually gain by upgrading, and which iPhones get the biggest improvements? Here’s what you need to know.


iOS 27 vs iOS 26: At a glance
iOS 27 may seem a little light on specific new features, with more focus seemingly given to performance, security and sorting out Siri. Here’s the main improvements Apple announced:
Is Siri better in iOS 27?
Yes: iOS 26 introduced Apple Intelligence features; iOS 27 transforms Siri into a contextual AI assistant with cross-app actions.
Has performance improved?
Yes: iOS 26 focused on features and redesigns; iOS 27 prioritises speed, responsiveness, stability and system optimisation.
What’s new for photos?
iOS 26 added Visual Intelligence screenshot analysis; iOS 27 adds generative editing, expansion and reframing tools.
What’s changed for parents?
iOS 26 introduced improved child protections; iOS 27 adds website approvals, category controls and enhanced monitoring.
Has the design changed?
iOS 26 introduced Liquid Glass; iOS 27 refines it with better readability, clarity and adjustable intensity controls.


						

							




						

							




iOS 27 vs iOS 26 comparison table


CategoryiOS 27iOS 26

SiriFull Siri AI with personal context, cross-app actions and conversational workflowsBasic Apple Intelligence integration, Live Translation, Visual Intelligence
PerformanceUp to 30% faster app launches, 70% faster photo loading, 80% faster AirDropStandard optimisation
DesignRefined Liquid Glass with improved readability and adjustable transparencyIntroduced Liquid Glass interface
PhotosAI image expansion, object removal, Reframe and enhanced Image PlaygroundVisual Intelligence screenshot analysis
PhoneCall Context surfaces relevant emails, messages and information during callsCall Screening, Hold Assist, voicemail summaries
SecurityAutomatic password replacement for compromised accountsPassword management improvements
Parental ControlsAsk to Browse, category-based limits and expanded safety protectionsAsk to Buy and Communication Safety
GamesLargely unchangedNew dedicated Games app
AI FeaturesNext-generation Apple Intelligence powered by Siri AI and Gemini integrationFirst wave of Apple Intelligence features
FocusAI, performance, security and reliabilityNew features and redesign

 






What are the best new features in iOS 27?

				
					

				
			
New features in iOS 27 

Foundry





Better Siri – Siri AI is the headline upgrade. It will understand personal context, search messages, photos and emails, perform actions across apps, follow conversational requests and remember previous interactions. It will be able to find information buried in your communications, create reminders and complete multi-step tasks without switching between apps.
Automatic fix for compromised passwords – One of the most practical additions. Siri will be able to identify compromised passwords stored in the Passwords app, sign into supported services, generate stronger replacements and save them automatically. If it works as demonstrated, it removes one of the biggest barriers to improving online security.
New AI photo editing features – Photos gains powerful generative editing tools. Users can expand image borders beyond the original frame, remove larger unwanted objects more naturally, and use Reframe to change image perspective while AI fills newly created areas. Image Playground also gains more advanced image generation and style transformations.
A faster iPhone – Apple says app launches are up to 30% faster, photo libraries load up to 70% quicker and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% faster. Unlike iOS 26’s feature-heavy release, iOS 27 puts significant emphasis on performance, stability and day-to-day responsiveness.
New safety features for families – Parental controls will become much more granular. Parents will be able to set separate limits for games, entertainment and social media, approve access to unfamiliar websites through Ask to Browse, and benefit from expanded Communication Safety protections that help block sexual or violent content.


						

							


When will iOS 27 be released?
Apple released iOS 27 on September 14, 2026, as a free software update for compatible iPhones.
The update includes most of the features Apple previewed at WWDC in June, including the new Siri AI, although availability varies by device, language and region. Siri AI is initially rolling out as a beta for supported devices set to English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish support due in October.


						

							


Which iPhones will support iOS 27?
iOS 27 is compatible with the following iPhones:
iPhone Duo
iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro
iPhone Air 
iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17, iPhone 17e
iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16, iPhone 16e
iPhone 15 Pro Max, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 15
iPhone 14 Pro Max, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 14 Plus, iPhone 14
iPhone 13 Pro Max, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 13, iPhone 13 mini
iPhone 12 Pro Max, iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 12, iPhone 12 mini
iPhone 11 Pro Max, iPhone 11 Pro, iPhone 11
iPhone SE (2nd & 3rd generation)
One thing to note is that the most advanced on-device AI models will be restricted to iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and iPhone 16 models or later. This is linked to the amount of RAM available, and you’ll only miss out on some of the new Siri voice models and dictation accuracy.


						

							


Everything new in iOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




When iOS 26 launched in September 2025, it introduced major changes including the Liquid Glass redesign, a revamped Phone app, and new Apple Intelligence features such as Call Screening, Live Translation, voicemail summaries and Hold Assist. Apple also added a dedicated Games app, redesigned the Camera app and expanded Visual Intelligence with screenshot analysis and ChatGPT integration. Read our comprehensive iOS 26 guide for more information. 
By comparison, iOS 27 focuses less on introducing entirely new features and more on improving Siri, boosting performance, enhancing security and expanding AI capabilities. Here are the biggest changes coming with iOS 27.


						

							


An even better Siri 
A beta version of Siri AI arrived in English alongside iOS 27 on September 14, with additional languages and broader availability to follow.
Apple’s new version of Siri is a major upgrade, although at launch the company is still describing Siri AI as a beta. The initial release brings more natural conversations, personal context, onscreen awareness, web answers, more powerful actions across apps, conversation history and improved writing tools. Some additional capabilities, including enhanced voices and dictation, require newer hardware.
The new models draw on two main sources of information: Personal Context, which uses relevant information stored on your iPhone, and Broad World Knowledge, which can pull in information from the web. Together, these are designed to give Siri a much better understanding of what you’re asking and what you want to do.
Thanks to deeper integration with iOS and apps such as Mail, Messages and Photos, Siri AI can do more than simply answer questions. It can understand information on your screen, use context from your communications and personal data, and suggest or carry out relevant actions across apps.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Say you exchange a few emails with a friend about a potential meet-up. Siri AI can surmise from the text what’s going on, then offer to create a Calendar entry for the relevant time and date, all without you needing to ask for anything. 
It should also be able to find photos or things mentioned in messages just by you asking it to track them down. For example, if someone sent you a message about a new TV show they thought you would like, but you can’t remember what it was, you can simply ask Siri AI ‘Hey, what TV show did Paul say I should watch?’, which will trigger a search through your conversations to find the answer. 
The new Siri AI functionality works across multiple Apple applications. For instance, in Apple’s example, Siri AI was asked when a certain performer’s concert is coming up. Then, it was asked how to buy tickets, with the answer showing that there was a lottery draw. Apple’s demonstrator then told Siri AI to set a reminder for when the lottery would begin, while also playing a song from the artist in Apple Music. This was all seamlessly in the conversation, rather than a separate set of tasks. 
In another example, Siri AI was asked where a contact’s new address was? This was found in a Message, then it was instructed to plot the journey there in Apple Maps, which it did without issue. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Other features include Call Context, where Siri will automatically bring any relevant information to your attention when you’re on a call with someone. So, if you call a builder you’ve arranged some work with, Siri will show you the emails exchanges and any other data it thinks you might need for the conversation.
There seems to be plenty of scope for the new Siri AI, and it will accessible either by the normal voice command, swiping down from the Dynamic Island or holding the Side Button for longer interactions. You’ll also be able to see all your previous interactions and conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, which syncs across all your Apple devices. 
The focus on this year seems to be more on making the basics work well and that could be what most people actually want. One caveat is that due to an ongoing disagreement with the EU over the Digital Markets Act, countries in the Union won’t be able to get Siri AI on iPhone or iPad at launch. 


						

							


Automatic password fix
While this falls into the standard remit of Siri AI, it does feel like it needs its own section. With its new powers, Apple’s digital assistant will be able to do something very useful. Provided you keep your login details to all your accounts and sites in the Apple Passwords app, you can instruct Siri to find any compromised passwords, log in to the revenant service and change them automatically to a new, safer one. These are then be stored in the Passwords app and your details would be secure once more. 

				
					

				
			
Siri will look after changing your password. 

Apple



							


New AI photo editing features
The new AI models in iOS 27 seem pretty impressive. You are able to take existing images and have Siri increase the area of the image by up to 25%, with the new surrounding parts auto-generated by the system to match the rest of the image. It’s like zooming out and finding that there’s more to the image than you first thought. 
You can also clean up parts of images with more powerful tools that can remove large objects while still persevering the look of the photo. Perhaps the most stunning though is Reframe, which lets you take an existing image and change its perspective, with the new areas filled in by AI generated content. Essentially, you can pan around the subject and Siri will magically make it look real. 

				
					

				
			
Use AI to make your photos even better.

Apple




Image Playground has also been revamped so you can create images from prompts as well as change photos into a variety of styles just by asking Siri AI. 


						

							


New child safety features
Apple takes privacy and safety seriously, and that extends to younger users. With iOS 27 you’ll have expanded control over Screen Time for your kids, with the three main areas of Entertainment, Games, and Social Media all having granular times limits and schedules that you can set to prevent little ones from spending too much time on their devices. 
Dedicated Child Accounts come with guidance on the kind of usage is heathy for children, with Apple working alongside the American Academy of Pediatrics to give parents and idea of what is appropriate for their kids. The controls also change as the child gets older, allowing my precise controls rather than blanket settings. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Alongside the Ask to Buy feature already present in iOS 26, where children can send a message to their parent asking permission to make app purchases, iOS 27 adds Ask to Browse, which prevents the child from opening a website they haven’t used before until they get permission. 
Communication Safety will now also monitor any messages coming in or out of the child’s device, preventing any sexual or violent images from being able to be seen, received or sent. 


						

							


Liquid Glass and design tweaks
One of the biggest changes in iOS 26 was the introduction of the Liquid Glass graphical interface. This wasn’t entirely met with cheers and adoration, so Apple has done some work and brings needed fixes in iOS 27. These include subtle redesigns, such as frosted menu bars across the top of sections of the interface where there are controls. This should help with legibility, as will some of the other colour and clarity adjustments that Apple announced. There will also be a slider in the Settings that allows you to manually change the level of the effect on the interface. 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Performance is set to get an upgrade too, with Apple promising plenty of enhancements to the underlying engine. It claims that iPhone apps will launch 30% faster, new photos load into libraries up to 70% quicker, and AirDrop gets the biggest boost as transfer times could be reduced by up to 80%.


						

							


What else is new? 
Since Apple first previewed iOS 27, we’ve learned more about some of the smaller improvements included in the final release. These include Enhanced Flyover in Maps, Custom EQ controls for AirPods, new Apple Intelligence features in the Home app, including smarter camera notifications and HomeKit Secure Video search, and GymKit support on the iPhone.
iOS 27 also introduces special interface features for Apple’s new iPhone Duo, including support for side-by-side apps and layouts that adapt as the foldable iPhone is opened, closed or repositioned. 


						

							


iOS 27 vs iOS 26: Is it worth upgrading?
Apple went hard on AI when the iPhone 16 launched, but the rollout of Apple Intelligence didn’t go as smoothly as expected, with some features delayed and others taking longer than anticipated to arrive.
With iOS 27, Apple is taking another big step toward delivering on that original promise. The biggest draw is the much smarter Siri, alongside new Apple Intelligence features, faster performance, stronger security and improvements across many of Apple’s apps.
If you have an iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, particularly an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model, iOS 27 should be a worthwhile upgrade. Older supported iPhones still benefit from many of the other improvements, but they miss out on some of the more advanced AI features.
For a more detailed look at everything included, see our comprehensive iOS 27 guide.

title: If you let it, Apple Intelligence will train itself on your data in iOS 27
content:
As it turns out, Apple realistically needs customer data to make Siri AI work well. So, starting with iOS 27, it is asking users to opt-in to training on your data.


Apple wants your Siri conversations
A new section in the iOS 27 privacy policy shows that Apple has reversed its stance on using customers' data to train its AI models. Previously, the company assured customers that it had no need for customer data, and would figure out how to make Siri AI work well without it.
Apple maintains that it "takes steps to ensure that personal data is not stored or used by Apple." But as Heise points out, and Apple has said in the terms of service for a few years now, the audio material may be listened to by Apple employees after anonymization.

title: How to create a bootable macOS USB installer for macOS 27 Golden Gate and older
content:
Macworld





Being able to create a bootable USB installer for macOS is a useful skill for any Mac user. Whether you’re performing a clean install, setting up multiple Macs, recovering a system that won’t boot, or simply want a reliable offline installer, a bootable USB drive gives you far more control than relying on macOS Recovery alone.
Creating a bootable installer is easier than it used to be thanks to Apple’s Terminal command, createinstallmedia, but the process still isn’t obvious – and it differs depending on whether you’re using an Intel Mac or a Mac with Apple silicon. You’ll need the correct macOS installer, a USB drive with enough capacity, and a few Terminal commands that need to be entered exactly.
In this guide, we’ll show you how to create a bootable USB installer for macOS Golden Gate, as well as macOS Tahoe, macOS Sequoia and older versions of macOS. We’ll explain what you need before you begin, how the process differs between Intel and Apple silicon Macs, and how to use your installer once it’s ready. By the end, you’ll have a reusable macOS installer that can save you time, bandwidth and frustration – and it might even help you recover a Mac when nothing else will.

How to create a bootable macOS Installer 
We will run through the following steps to create a bootable USB for Mac:
Get the macOS installer files

What you need to make a bootable USB for Mac
A 32GB Flash Drive (Minimum): To create a bootable USB installer, you typically need a USB flash drive or Thunderbolt drive with at least 16GB (we recommend 32GB) of space. Using a faster drive, such as a USB 3.0 or USB-C stick, is recommended to reduce installation times. 

Note: If you have data on the drive that you plan to use you will need to transfer it to another drive, as it will be completely formatted and erased.
macOS installation files: You can obtain these from the Mac App Store, Software Update in System Settings, or other official Apple sources.
A Compatible Mac.
Admin access: You will need to have an admin user account on the Mac you are working with. 
Internet access: It goes without saying that you will need an internet connection to download the software and you may need it while installing the version of macOS if it needs to check for firmware or confirm your iCloud credentials.


						

							






						

							
1.
Get the macOS installer files

				
					

				
			
You can get installers from the Mac App Store – as long as your Mac is compatible.

Foundry






How you get the installation files will depend on the version you want the installer for. Below we’ll look at how to get various macOS installers. If it’s an older version you are after, we have a dedicated article about How to download old Mac OS X and macOS versions.
Warning: Download the installation files, but make sure you stop before the actual installation starts. When the installation starts the files will be disposed of, so you need to step in beforehand!
Where to get macOS Golden Gate installer: From September 14, macOS Golden Gate can be downloaded on compatible Macs through the Software Update mechanism within macOS. Navigate to the Apple menu > System Settings > General > Software Update. Your Mac will check for the latest version, and you can click Upgrade Now to begin the download.
Where to get the macOS beta: To get the latest beta files you need to first register for the Apple’s official developer or public beta programs. You can then download the latest beta from Software Update, as described above. See: Latest macOS beta details and how to get it.
Where to get other macOS installers: You can download the installers from these Mac App Store links. Make sure you use Safari and close the Mac App Store before clicking on the link or it may not work. If your Mac is too new it may not be compatible with these older versions. 
macOS Tahoe
macOS Sequoia
macOS Sonoma
macOS Ventura
macOS Monterey
macOS Big Sur
macOS Catalina 
macOS Mojave
macOS High Sierra
Once the installation files are downloaded you will be able to find them in the Applications folder via the Finder. Now you have the installation files, we can move on to the process of making the bootable installer.
Creating a bootable installation of macOS requires a single command in Terminal (this has been the case since Mavericks arrived in 2013). The createinstallmedia command makes it possible to create a bootable copy of an installer on any drive that’s connected to your Mac. You’ll find all the createinstallmedia commands at the bottom of this article.
Warning: The createinstallmedia command erases anything on the external disk you use for your bootable drive, so make sure there’s nothing on it that you need.

						

							
2.
Connect and prepare the drive manually, if necessary

				
					

				
			
Using Disk Utility to prepare the hard drive. 

Foundry






You may not need to prepare the drive manually. If everything in step 3 (below) works as expected, the createinstallmedia command will erase the external drive and format it as Mac OS Extended (Journaled) automatically. You can therefore skip these Disk Utility steps and go straight to creating the bootable installer. However, if createinstallmedia can’t erase or prepare the drive correctly, we recommend formatting it manually first using the steps below.
Connect a USB flash drive or other external drive with at least 32GB of space. Everything on the drive will be erased, so make a copy of anything you want to keep first.
Open Disk Utility (press Command + spacebar and start to type Disk Utility).
In Disk Utility click View and select Show All Devices.
From the sidebar, physical external drive itself, rather than one of the volumes underneath it.
Click Erase.
Give the drive a simple name such as MyVolume. You can use another name, but you must use that exact name later in the Terminal command.
Set Scheme to GUID Partition Map. Note that createinstallmedia will ultimately erase the drive as Mac OS Extended (Journaled).
Click Erase, wait for Disk Utility to finish, then click Done. 

						

							
3.
Create the bootable macOS installer

				
					

				
			
Use Terminal to create your installer.

Foundry






Before starting this part of the process, make sure the full macOS installer is in your Applications folder. If you ran the update when you downloaded it the installer will need to be downloaded again. 
Open Terminal (Command + Space and type Terminal).
Enter the createinstallmedia command for the version of macOS you want to install. You can find the commands at the bottom of this article. 
Press Return.
Enter your administrator password when prompted. Nothing will appear on screen while you type the password; this is normal.
If macOS asks Terminal for permission to access the removable drive, click OK.
When Terminal warns that the drive will be erased, type Y and press Return.
Wait while Terminal erases the drive and copies the macOS installer. This may take several minutes. When it is finished you should see “Copy complete. Done.” 
The external drive is now a bootable macOS installer.

						

							
4.
Boot the Mac from the installer

				
					

				
			
Foundry






This process is different on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
On an Apple Silicon Mac:
Connect the installer drive and shut down the Mac.
Press and hold the power button until Startup Options appears.
Select the macOS installer.
Click Continue.
On an Intel Mac:
Connect the installer drive and shut down the Mac.
Turn it on while holding the Option/Alt key.
Select the macOS installer from the startup menu.
Press Return or choose Continue.
Note: Apple warns that Macs with a T2 Security Chip may need Startup Security Utility configured to allow booting from external or removable media.

						

							
5.
Install macOS

				
					

				
			
Install the version of macOS you want.

Foundry






Once the Mac has started from the USB installer, choose the option to Install macOS and follow the onscreen instructions. 
The installer can only install that version of macOS on Macs that support it.
If you want a clean install, you must first erase the Mac’s internal disk before installing macOS; otherwise, you can install the OS normally without wiping the Mac. Read How to clean install macOS for step-by-step instructions.

						

							
createinstallmedia commands 
The createinstallmedia command will be slightly different depending on which version of macOS you are wanting to use.
Note MyVolume may have a different name for you, for example it might be USB or Untitled. Check in Disk Utilities, it’s the name of the external disk you are using.
WARNING: We have heard of people copying and pasting in the -- only for them to change to a – in Terminal, so be careful of that. There should be two dashes!

title: Your old iPhone is actually going to get faster this week
content:
Macworld





The main highlight of iOS 27, launching on September 14, will be artificial intelligence, which is only available on relatively new phones (iPhone 15 Pro, and iPhone 16 and later). Head over to the iOS 27 site on Apple.com, and you’ll see a lot about the new Siri AI, Apple Intelligence, and other features that require the latest hardware to run. Unsurprisingly, this might leave owners of older iPhones wondering what exactly they’ll gain from the update.
After spending some time testing the iOS 27 beta on an iPhone 11 Pro Max (the oldest iPhone supported by the update), I can report that iOS 27 is just as important for older iPhones—maybe even more so. Although they’ll miss out on the latest AI features, iOS 27 may be the best update older iPhones have received in years.
iOS 27 makes older iPhones fast again
If you’ve installed iOS 26 on an older iPhone, you’ve probably noticed that some things weren’t exactly smooth. Even some of the latest iPhones had some trouble running the fancy animations added with Liquid Glass.
Earlier this year, I wrote about how iOS 26 seemed noticeably buggy compared to other recent iOS releases. Animations stuttered more often, apps took longer to launch, and even basic system interactions sometimes felt sluggish.
Apple promised that iOS 27 would address many of these issues. Even before the release candidate arrived this week, my tests with the iPhone 11 Pro Max show that the company was serious about improving performance, especially when it comes to old hardware.

				
					

				
			
iOS 27 will bring some design refinements to Liquid Glass, but the real improvements are with performance.

Foundry




To get a better idea of how much has changed, I measured the time it takes to complete a handful of common tasks on the same iPhone 11 Pro Max running iOS 26 and iOS 27 beta 1.
I started with something simple that most people do every day: taking photos with their iPhone. On iOS 26, my iPhone 11 took 0.98 seconds to open the Camera app, then 3.61 seconds to take a photo and load it into my photo library.
I ran the test again with iOS 27, and the improvements were noticeable. Now it only takes about 0.65 seconds to open the Camera app, and 2.44 seconds to take a photo and immediately open it from the thumbnail preview. For users, this means a lower chance of missing an important shot because their phone is too slow.
Many iPhone users also rely on the Maps app every day, and on iOS 26, the iPhone 11 took a long 3.01 seconds to load it. With the first beta of iOS 27, the same iPhone now loads the Maps app in just 1.36 seconds. That’s twice as fast as on iOS 26.
Other actions, such as launching Safari, browsing the App Store, and opening the share sheet, are also noticeably faster in iOS 27. 

iOS 27 beta vs. iOS 26 speed tests

		
			


Results are in seconds. Lower results/shorter bars are better.




On their own, these numbers won’t transform the experience. After all, we’re talking about fractions of a second in some cases. But when you’re running these tasks multiple times a day, every second adds up to minutes saved. And the whole system feels remarkably faster.
The smoother animations matter even more
Performance benchmarks are only part of the story. What really makes iOS 27 better on the iPhone 11 is how much smoother the animations feel during everyday use.
Visuals everywhere appear more consistent and less prone to frame drops. Swiping to open Control Center is noticeably more fluid. Unlocking the phone feels more responsive. App transitions seem better optimized and less likely to hitch. 
Those were all things that bothered me when I tried using this iPhone on iOS 26, and now Apple seems to have fixed nearly all of the slow animations.
Once again, these aren’t dramatic changes individually, but together they create the impression that the old hardware is no longer struggling to keep up with the operating system. The result is an iPhone that feels newer than it actually is.

				
					

				
			
You won’t get all of the features that you get on the iPhone 17 PRI Max, but iOS 27 will still be an impressive upgrade for older iPhones.

Foundry




iOS 27 also runs cooler
Another change I noticed almost immediately is the temperature. While my iPhone 11 Pro Max heats up quite easily on iOS 26, even when performing basic tasks, iOS 27 seems to keep the phone cool for longer. And that’s a great sign that the optimizations Apple made across the system have worked.
A cooler phone generally indicates that software processes are being managed more efficiently. It often means less unnecessary CPU and GPU activity, which can also translate into better battery life over time.
What’s more, these numbers were from one of the earlier betas, so it’s likely that the version Apple ships Monday will be even better for battery life.
Older iPhones are getting a lot
If you watched the WWDC keynote, you might have been disappointed, as it seemed as though older iPhones wouldn’t be getting anything more than bug fixes with iOS 27. But that’s not actually the case. In fact, while devices like the iPhone 11 won’t support Siri AI, there are still many other new features coming to these devices.
One of my favorite new features in iOS 27 is the new clipboard shortcut right on the keyboard, which makes it faster to paste text or even a screenshot you just took. Being able to control the volume of the alarms and timers independently was also a nice addition.

				
					

				
			
Older iPhones won’t miss out on small iOS 27 features like this clipboard upgrade in the keyboard.

Foundry




There’s also the ability to create custom passes in the Wallet app, a redesigned interface that makes it easier to play audio messages in iMessage, an option to save a high-resolution frame from a video in the Photos app, and larger Home Screen widgets.
All of these features are coming to older iPhones with iOS 27. Sure, they might not sound as exciting as a new AI assistant that can control your phone, but they’re exactly the kind of improvements that make your phone feel more useful and polished.
Not to mention that all iPhones getting iOS 27 will feature refinements to the Liquid Glass interface, including the new transparency slider that lets you choose the look you want.
iOS 27 is a surprisingly great update for aging iPhones
To be honest, I was quite surprised when Apple confirmed that even the iPhone 11 would get the iOS 27 update. After all, my experience running iOS 26 on that generation of phone was quite frustrating. But now that I’ve tried the first beta, I can see why Apple made that decision.
The main narrative surrounding iOS 27 focuses heavily on AI, and that’s completely understandable. Apple had been lagging behind in this race, so it’s no surprise that they want to make a big deal out of all the new Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features.

				
					

				
			
Don’t worry about missing out on Siri AI. iOS 27 is a fantastic upgrade for older iPhones.

Foundry




Yet, after using iOS 27 on an iPhone 11 Pro Max, I can’t help but think that older devices may be among the biggest beneficiaries of this update. The software feels faster. Animations are smoother. The phone runs cooler. And users still get a collection of useful new features despite missing out on AI.
For anyone worried that iOS 27 would leave older iPhones behind, the first beta suggests the opposite. Apple appears to have spent just as much time optimizing the experience for existing users as it did building features for future hardware, and that’s great news for people still holding onto a seven-year-old iPhone.

title: Apple apparently doesn’t want you hanging out at its stores anymore
content:
Macworld





The reign of new CEO John Ternus has only just got underway, but Apple is already plotting a major revamp to its retail strategy.
According to the latest instalment of Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter, the company is preparing a “retail store shake-up” that will see its brick-and-mortar outlets shift focus from so-called “community landmarks” and gathering places towards “more traditional and practical” retail spaces. The priority, it would appear, will be on encouraging customers to buy rather than to connect with the community.
The revamp will feature three major changes, Gurman describes. Dedicated Genius Bars will return. The giant video walls currently found in some outlets will vanish. And the “Avenue” sections along the sides of Apple stores will be redesigned and repurposed for collection of online purchases and hosting “Today at Apple” workshops. New fixtures for the Genius Bars and redesigned Avenues will be made entirely from wood, Gurman reports, while looking “fully integrated–as if they had been part of the original design.”
The presence of Genius Bars and the continuation of Today at Apple sessions indicates that the company hasn’t completely given up on its strategy of encouraging customers to visit for reasons other than making a purchase. But such hosting, helping, and community functions are reportedly set to become a lower priority, in stark contrast to the Apple store’s founding principles.
 It isn’t clear why Apple wants to move in a different direction now. In 2001 Ron Johnson envisaged the stores as hubs for the Apple user community, and he even modelled early examples on public buildings such as libraries, rather than rival shops. Angela Ahrendts and Jony Ive later evolved the concept as a high-concept luxury space and statement of the company’s aesthetic values: a town hall for likeminded people. This was a risky and unusual approach, but it paid off. (Johnson’s and Ahrendts’ retail efforts each landed them spots in our rundown of the 50 most important people in Apple’s history.) 
Gurman adds that Apple is bringing in stricter rules for its retail employees, who have complained about conditions in the past and may be surprised to hear that stricter rules are necessary. Staff will be required to stand throughout pre-opening meetings, he says, and will be forbidden from drinking or looking at devices, and must “stay fully engaged.” When doors open, every staff member will be required to applaud the first customers. It’s debatable whether they will be in the mood to applaud after hearing about the new rules.

title: Apple Stores Said to Lose Video Walls, Regain Dedicated Genius Bars
content:
Apple is working on a sweeping retail overhaul that would bring back dedicated Genius Bars to its stores, carve out new spaces for order pickup and Today at Apple classes, and do away with oversized video walls, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


In this week's "Power On" newsletter, Gurman said that Apple intends to speed up store renovations over the coming years. Apple plans to rework the "Avenue," its term for the side sections of a store where accessories and services are displayed, reinstate standalone Genius Bars, and remove the large video screens installed in many locations.

Pickup and Today at Apple, which typically share a counter and a seating area today, will each get their own compact section along the Avenue, described internally as a "bay" and measuring about 10 feet across.

For pickup, Gurman described plans for an all-wood bay with a faint Apple logo worked into the upper section, with lockable drawers underneath for holding customer orders, fronted by a counter where staff can hand items over. The Today at Apple bay will feature a similar look, topped by a display similar to a large television, with drawers below for stashing iPads, laptops, and other class equipment, plus a fixed instructor table and stools nearby.

The video walls being phased out trace back to the retail vision pursued under former retail chief Angela Ahrendts, who treated Apple stores as public gathering places rather than purely transactional spaces. Gurman frames the current shift as a move away from that toward stores built primarily around service, fulfillment, and everyday shopping needs.

Where those screens come down, most stores will gain a wood finished Genius Bar built to echo the design Apple used before it introduced the open plan "Genius Grove." It includes counters set at two different heights for accessibility, backed by a wall of storage drawers and large product imagery. Gurman added that both the new bars and the Avenue bays are meant to look as though they always belonged in the store, rather than as visible retrofits, and that many renovated locations will also see their break rooms and other back-of-house areas refurbished.

Elements of the redesign are already live in a small number of stores around the world. Gurman expects the fuller version of the proposed store overhaul to reach most newly opened and renovated stores gradually, with the international rollout continuing over several years.

Is your iPhone still supported by Apple?

				
					

				
			Comparing iPhone 12 mini and iPhone SE.
Michael Simon/IDG




As of September 14, 2026, the current iPhone operating system is iOS 27. But even if your iPhone can’t run the latest version of iOS, it can still be safe to use as long as Apple continues to provide security updates for it. Apple regularly releases updates for older versions of iOS to patch vulnerabilities, including flaws that are being actively exploited.
For example, in March 2026 the “DarkSword” hacking toolkit was identified as targeting iPhones running older versions of iOS 18. The security vulnerabilities exploited by DarkSword had already been addressed in the iOS 18.7.6 update.
If you use an iPhone running a version of iOS that Apple no longer supports with security updates, you are at greater risk from attacks that exploit vulnerabilities in older software.
Some updates may also be required to maintain certificates used by essential services such as iMessage, FaceTime, and device activation. If your iPhone is running an unsupported version of iOS, you may eventually find that some of these features stop working.
The good news is that all of the iPhone models listed in the table above are currently receiving some level of support from Apple, although the type of support varies.
Apple continues to provide security updates for several older versions of iOS:
Apple issued iOS 16.7.16 with security updates for the iPhone 8 and iPhone X in May 2026.
Apple issued iOS 15.8.8 with security updates for the iPhone 6s, iPhone 7, and first-generation iPhone SE in May 2026.
Apple issued iOS 18.7.9 with security updates specifically for the iPhone XS and XR generation in May 2026.
Apple issued iOS 18.7.10 with security updates for the iPhone XS and XR in August 2026..
Apple doesn’t need to maintain iOS 17 as a separate security-update branch because every iPhone capable of running iOS 17 can upgrade to a newer version of iOS.
This means that, for now at least, the following older iPhones are still receiving security updates:
iPhone X
iPhone 8 and 8 Plus
iPhone 7 and 7 Plus
iPhone SE (1st generation)
iPhone 6s and 6s Plus — the oldest supported iPhones
We don’t know how much longer Apple will continue to support iOS 15 and iOS 16 — and, by extension, the iPhones that depend on them. As we explain in How long Apple supports iPhones for, Apple gradually moves older products through its vintage and obsolete classifications, while software security support can continue on a different timetable.


						

							


Should I upgrade my iPhone?

				
					

				
			
IDG




If your iPhone can’t run the newest version of iOS, that doesn’t necessarily mean you need to upgrade. While you won’t get the latest features, Apple continues to issue software updates that address security vulnerabilities in older versions of iOS. During 2026, Apple supported iOS 18, iOS 16 and iOS 15 with security updates, extending support to iPhones ranging from 2015’s iPhone 6s to 2018’s iPhone XR and iPhone XS.
However, if you’re using an older iPhone, security is the key concern. Apple is still providing security patches for devices running iOS 15 and iOS 16, but this support is unlikely to continue indefinitely. Now that iOS 27 has arrived, these older versions are increasingly likely to reach the end of security support.
By contrast, iOS 18 support is expected to continue for some time, extending the usable life of the iPhone XS and XR.
Once your device can no longer run a supported version of iOS, it’s time to seriously consider upgrading. We explain how long Apple supports the iPhone for in a separate article, and you can see full iOS compatibility in the table above.patibility in the table above.
As a general rule, any iPhone that can’t run iOS 27 is approaching the end of its practical lifespan, even if Apple is still providing security updates for it.
Even among iPhones that do support iOS 27, there are good reasons to consider upgrading. In particular, many older models don’t support Apple Intelligence and other newer features that depend on more recent hardware.
If you own one of the following iPhones, upgrading to a recent model such as the iPhone 18 could bring significantly improved performance, cameras, battery life and access to newer features:

If you’re not sure which version of iOS you’re currently running, it’s very easy to find out. 
Open Settings.
Tap on General.
Tap About and look for the iOS Version number.

Now that you know the latest version of iOS that your iPhone supports, it’s a good idea to make sure you’re running on that platform. 
Updating iOS on an iPhone is simple, follow these steps:

title: Apple's Siri AI Can Be Swapped Out for Claude, ChatGPT, Code Shows
content:
Code sleuth "pdfu" has uncovered iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate private frameworks that show Apple has designed its new Siri architecture to work with third-party AI models at what appears to be a surprisingly deep level.


One mechanism called Model Delegation allows Claude to appear as a Siri extension in the same way as the existing built-in ChatGPT extension. In pdfu's video, shared on X, the macOS user brings up the "Search or Ask" bar and chooses Claude as the AI model via an "Ask..." contextual menu. 

After enabling the Claude extension, the user asks Siri to "Ask Claude" to set a reminder in Apple's Reminders app. Claude then interprets the natural language reminder request and Siri subsequently creates the reminder. The implication is that if the request requires access to an Apple system feature, Claude hands the task back to Siri. 

In another example, Claude can be seen in a Siri app conversation window receiving a request to create a CSV file – something Siri itself cannot handle – and successfully returning the result. 

What's more intriguing is the second protocol demonstrated in the video that appears to go considerably further, and could really open up the AI landscape for Apple software requests. 

An inference provider in "Model Manager Services" apparently allows Apple's own server-side Siri model to be completely replaced by another model, such as GPT-5.6. In this scenario, ChatGPT receives Apple's Siri planner prompt and tool definitions, which enables it to request system actions, receive the resulting personal data, and formulate an answer that Siri presents using its own interface and voice. 


And here's an app extension replacing Siri AI's server model with GPT-5.6 Terra. It uses the Inference Providing protocol in Model Manager Services.
GPT-5.6 receives Apple's native Siri planner prompt and tool definitions. It can make tool calls that perform system actions, and... pic.twitter.com/cz88kyq3io
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 13, 2026
  

In the demonstration video, the user asks the ChatGPT model (within the Siri app) to find emails about a specific topic, summarize their contents and action points, then send a message to a person in the user's contacts via the Messages app. The response is then shown as logged in OpenAI's platform web interface.

The European Union's Digital Markets Act may have helped shape Apple's approach here, as it requires Apple to give third parties effective access to iOS hardware and software features available to Apple's own services, and the European Commission has specifically said this principle extends to Siri.

title: iPhone 18 Pro vs. iPhone 18 Pro Max Buyer's Guide
content:
Apple recently unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, featuring a new Main camera with a variable aperture, new Pro camera controls, the A20 Pro chip, and more. With the foldable iPhone Duo now sitting above them in the lineup, the two Pro models are no longer the most expensive iPhones Apple sells, but they remain the most fully-featured traditional iPhones available.


The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ starts at $1,199 and the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max starts at $1,299. Both see a $100 increase over the equivalent iPhone 17 Pro models, and the increases grow steeper further up the storage ladder, with a 1TB ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ now costing $300 more than a 1TB ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ did last year.

OLED Super Retina XDR always-on display with ProMotion and the Dynamic Island, the A20 Pro chip, 5G connectivity, a 48 megapixel Pro Fusion camera system, and the same four color options. Both are also offered in the same four storage tiers, including a 2TB option that is available on the smaller Pro model for the first time. Although the two phones share the vast majority of features, there are eight differences between the devices.

Our guide highlights the crucial differences between the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two iPhone models is best for you. Both models share the same thickness of 0.34 inches (8.75 mm), but otherwise have very different sizes and weights.

U.S. units of the larger model instead contain a Qualcomm modem, and iOS code seen points to the same radio used in last year's ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ models, which would make it the Snapdragon X80. 
 
The C2 supports both sub-6GHz and mmWave 5G, as the Qualcomm part does, and Apple says it is faster and more energy efficient than the C1X while adding AI-driven improvements to cellular quality and reliability. Real-world comparisons will not be possible until reviewers test both radios on the same networks. The clearest hint that the hardware genuinely differs is in the band listings, where the U.S. ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ supports LTE Band 106 and the U.S. ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max does not.

The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max represents the most you can get out of a traditional iPhone with the best possible battery life, but that does not necessarily translate into a worthwhile purchase for all users. At 8.78 ounces (249 grams), it is heavier than any iPhone Pro Max that came before it, and with a 6.9-inch display it is a large and hefty device.
 
Some may find the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max's size excessive or uncomfortably large to hold, while others will love the larger display for consuming media. Screen size is ultimately a matter of personal preference, and since the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max share all of their other features, it comes down to individual taste.
 
Battery life is the one area where the gap between the two models has widened meaningfully this year. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max gained six additional hours of video playback over the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max, while the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ gained three. The result is a nine-hour advantage for the larger model, up from six hours in the previous generation. If getting through a long day without reaching for a charger is your priority, the case for the Pro Max is more persuasive than it has been for some time.
 
The added $100 in price for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max seems fair for its additional display area and battery life, but it is important to weigh up these factors in your personal use-case. That $100 premium holds at every storage tier, so the larger model never becomes proportionally more expensive as capacity rises. Both devices become costly quickly with added storage, though, and the 1TB and 2TB tiers now carry surcharges that are considerably steeper than in previous years.
 
U.S. buyers have one extra factor to bear in mind. Choosing the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max in the United States means giving up Apple's own modem, and while the day-to-day difference is likely to be very small, it is an unusual position for the more expensive device to be in. If you specifically want the C2 and you are buying in the U.S., the smaller model is the only way to get it.
